transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in today?

Um… I guess what made me come in is my eating has been getting kind of out of hand. Like after work, or after class, I’ll sit down with my laptop to do emails or watch something, and then I end up eating a whole takeout meal, plus chips, sweets, and whatever random snacks I have in my desk drawer. I keep snacks there because sometimes I’m too busy to grab lunch, but then it’s like… I go through all of it.

It’s way more than I planned to eat, and definitely more than I’d eat if someone else were around. I just feel embarrassed about it, I guess, and I wasn’t sure if I should talk to someone.
After these episodes of eating more than you plan, do you ever try to make up for it by making yourself sick, using laxatives, or exercising a lot more than usual?

Um… I don’t really know. Like, I feel guilty after, and sometimes I’ll think I should “fix it” somehow, but I don’t—I mean, not in some organized way. I’ve never really thought of it like that.

I guess I mostly just feel gross and try to get back to normal the next day. Sorry, I’m kind of rambling—when you said exercising a lot, I started thinking about this one roommate I had who was super intense about the gym, like she’d plan her whole week around it, and I’m definitely not like that.
When you find yourself eating more than you planned, do you feel like you can't stop or control how much you're eating?

Yeah… I think that’s kind of the scariest part. Like once I start, it feels like I’m sort of watching myself keep reaching for the next thing, even while I’m thinking, Jaime, stop, you still have that budget report to finish and you’re not even enjoying this anymore.

And then I’ll be like, okay, after this handful I’m done, but then I’m opening something else. It’s weird because at work I’m usually pretty organized with numbers and deadlines and stuff, but with this it just feels like I can’t get a handle on it in the moment.
Do you find yourself eating this way mostly when you're alone because you're embarrassed about how much you're eating?

Yeah… mostly, yeah. I’ll kind of wait until my roommate is out, or if I’m home, until my family’s gone to bed. It’s embarrassing, because during the day I feel like I’m acting so put-together, like I’m careful and health-conscious and all that, and then I don’t want anyone seeing me eat that much.

I mean, my roommate is barely even home sometimes because she has this whole lab schedule and then she’ll go see her boyfriend, and I’ll notice I’m kind of… tracking when the apartment is empty. Not in a creepy way, just like, okay, now nobody’s here. And then it feels safer to do it, I guess.
When you’re having one of these episodes, do you find yourself eating much more quickly than normal?

Um… I don’t know if I’ve really noticed the speed part. I mean, it probably feels rushed in my head, but I’m not sure if I’m actually eating faster than normal, if that makes sense.

Like, I’m not sitting there timing myself or anything. Sometimes I’m more just distracted, and then suddenly I realize a lot is gone. Sorry—that probably doesn’t answer it very cleanly.
During these episodes, do you find yourself eating until you feel uncomfortably full, even if you didn’t really mean to?

Yeah… that does happen. Like by the end I’ll realize I’m really, really full, not just normal full. My stomach feels tight, like especially if I’m still in my work pants, and then I just kind of sit there for a while.

It’s embarrassing because I’ll think, okay, I need to get up and clean this up or do something productive, but if I move around too much or bend over I feel kind of sick. Like I didn’t mean to get to that point, but then suddenly I’m there.
Do you ever find yourself eating even when you’re not really hungry, like starting to eat just because you feel like it even if you haven’t skipped a meal or gone a long time without food?

Yeah… actually a lot of the time it’s not because I’m hungry. It’ll be right after dinner, which is the weird part, because I know I just ate and I’m not physically hungry.

But my brain feels kind of restless, like I can’t settle down, and then I’ll end up going back into the kitchen or looking at food delivery apps. Sometimes I tell myself I’m just checking what’s available, which sounds dumb when I say it out loud, but then it turns into ordering something anyway.
Do these episodes of eating this way cause you a lot of distress, or interfere with things like work, relationships, or how you see yourself?

Yeah… I think it does. I mean, I still get to work and school and everything, so from the outside it probably looks fine. But I’ve been kind of avoiding people more.

Like my friends will do these cooking nights or my family will ask me to come over for dinner, and I’ll make up excuses because I’m worried they’ll somehow notice. Not even during the meal, exactly, more like… I’m scared they’ll realize how much I’ve been eating when I’m by myself. Which sounds paranoid maybe, but it makes me not want to be around people.

So yeah, I guess I’ve been more isolated outside of work and classes. I just go home more than I used to.
How often do these episodes happen—like, would you say they occur at least once a week or more?

Yeah… I think it’s at least once a week. Honestly, when I was trying to convince myself it wasn’t that often, I went back through my journal and then my food delivery charges, because I’m weirdly better at tracking money than feelings.

And it was kind of obvious once I looked at it. Since the restructuring started, it’s been happening most weeks, and usually more than once a week. Not just like a random bad night here or there. I kept wanting to explain it away as, like, “Oh, that was a stressful day,” but then there were a lot of them.
Do you often feel ashamed or guilty after these episodes of eating, like you did something you shouldn’t have?

I mean… I don’t know if I’d use those exact words every time. Sometimes I’m more just annoyed with myself, like, “Why did I do that?” But then I start thinking about how much money I spent, because I’m weird about budgeting, and I’ll open my banking app and sort of stare at it like that’s going to undo anything.

Sorry, that’s not really answering. I guess there are times I feel bad afterward, yeah, but it’s kind of mixed up with being frustrated and wanting to pretend it didn’t happen.
